questions.q: What is the correct order of the five-step Chapter 3 method?
options: Ship it, design it, test it, document it, translate the complaint
Translate the complaint, design, document, test, ship
Test it, ship it, design it, document it, translate the complaint
Document it, ship it, test it, design it, translate the complaint
questions.explain: Each step depends on the one before it -- you can't document a design that hasn't been made, or test automation that hasn't been documented as intended.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say skipping straight from step 1 to step 5 is risky?
options: Because Salesforce blocks that sequence technically
Because step 5 cannot be performed without a paid license
It's exactly how undocumented, untested automation happens in the first place
There is no risk -- steps 2 through 4 are purely optional
questions.explain: The chapter's throughline is that documentation and testing aren't extra overhead -- they're what makes shipping safe.

questions.q: According to the automation health-check, what should you be able to do with an entry criteria?
options: State it without opening Setup
Delete it without review
Hide it from all other admins
Change it without testing
questions.explain: If the entry criteria can only be understood by opening Setup and reverse-engineering it, that's a documentation gap the health-check is meant to catch.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue the Chapter 3 method applies beyond the fictional case studies used to teach it?
options: Because the method only works for discount approvals specifically
Because fictional companies require a different method than real ones
The method does not apply outside of this course's exercises
Because the method doesn't change when the company and complaint are real instead of fictional
questions.explain: Complaint, requirements, design, documentation, and testing describe ordinary day-to-day administrator work, not a special advanced case.

questions.q: What does the health-check ask regarding test coverage specifically?
options: Whether the automation has ever been tested at all, in any form
Whether it's been tested against all four categories from Lesson 15, or only the happy path
Whether the automation has a custom icon
Whether the automation was built by an administrator or a developer
questions.explain: A single successful happy-path run is explicitly called out as insufficient on its own throughout this chapter.
